steps.content: The idea says: when a coin's daily dollar volume peaks relative to its own recent past, it tends to give some back. So the quantity is the recent-high ratio of `quote_volume` to its own 20-day average, and the sign must be negative. I'll start with the simplest version: the 5-day average of the 5-day high over the 20-day average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0321
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0209 (t = 7.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0331, 2023 +0.0235, 2024 +0.0121

The first version works: incremental IC +0.0209 with t = 7.1, and all three sub-periods point the same way, so the direction matches the idea. The ratio is a bounded, unit-free quantity, so it compares cleanly across coins. Since the peak is a single day, a 5-day average over a 5-day high is the cleanest way to express "just hit a recent high" without letting one noisy day dominate, and the 20-day baseline captures "recent" rather than the last few days.

I'll submit that one rather than spend another test on a more complex smoothing or window.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_max(window=5, min_periods=4).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16))</factor>

The idea is about dollar-volume level, not recent change: coins with low quote_volume should do better. The simplest, level form is the negative of the 20-day average of log quote_volume, which is comparable across coins and points the bearish way.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

The level form works in raw rank IC (+0.0371) but carries essentially nothing after the known styles are removed (+0.0011), and the sign flips in 2024. So the level level is mostly re-reading liquidity, which is already subtracted. Next I test a short, relative version of the same quantity: the 5-day log change in dollar volume, negated so that quiet coins score high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0131
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0067, 2023 -0.0003, 2024 -0.0002

The 5-day change is also flat (+0.0011) and its sign flips in 2024, so two tests in a row have failed to improve on the best result by any meaningful margin. I stop here and hand in the first, simplest version, which has the highest raw rank IC and the most even period split.

What I found: the level of dollar volume does carry information in raw rank IC (+0.0371), but almost all of it is the known liquidity level, which is already subtracted, so the incremental IC is small and the 2024 period even turns slightly negative. Replacing it with a short 5-day change or a 20-day relative change changes nothing, so the level level is the honest, if modest, measurement of the idea on this history. I keep the bearish sign the idea asks for, and I hand in the simplest form.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16).ln()</factor>
The idea is a one-day ratio: close above open, so the simplest form is (close − open)/close, no sign flip because the idea is bullish. I'll start with that single-day version, smoothed over 5 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0370
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0004 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0010, 2023 +0.0006, 2024 +0.0000

The raw level is essentially flat (incremental IC 0.0004, t=1.9) and the sign flips between periods, so a single day's gap is too noisy. I'll keep the same quantity but smooth it over 20 days instead, which should make it less a single-day noise and more of a persistent "tendency to close above open".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0446
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0084 (t = -3.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0081, 2023 -0.0146, 2024 -0.0023

Smoothing over 20 days makes it clearly negative (incremental IC −0.0084, t = −3.6, negative in all three periods), so the persistent level of the gap is bearish on this history. That is two tests in a row that failed to beat the first result by any meaningful margin, so I'll stop and hand in the first form.

What I found: the plain one-day gap (close above open) carries essentially no incremental information once liquidity, volatility, reversal and 30-day momentum are removed (incremental IC 0.0004, t = 1.9, positive in all three sub-periods but small). Smoothing it over 20 days instead of 5 flips the sign to bearish and is worse in every sub-period, so I keep the short-window version that at least keeps the direction the idea states.

<factor>(Factor('close') - Factor('open')).safe_div(Factor('close')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is a single-day ratio: close over open, which is a ratio of two prices and so is comparable across coins regardless of their price unit. Since the idea says the ratio is bullish, the factor is that ratio itself, with no sign flip. I'll start with the simplest form: the 1-day return.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0000 (t = -0.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0001, 2023 +0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The 1-day ratio is essentially the short-term reversal style, which is already subtracted out, so incremental IC is exactly 0.0000 with a t of −0.0 and no period carries any signal. To keep the same quantity (close above open) but measure it over a few days instead of one, I'll smooth the ratio with a 5-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0400
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0003 (t = -1.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0010, 2023 +0.0002, 2024 -0.0004

Smoothing made it slightly worse (−0.0003, t = −1.3) and the sign flips across periods, so two forms in a row failed to improve on the first. I'll stop testing and hand in the simplest form, which is the one that matches the idea most literally and has the least negative absolute IC.

What I found: the quantity the idea names — the close-to-open ratio — is essentially the short-term reversal style, which is already removed from the incremental IC, so its incremental content is essentially zero. The raw rank IC is negative (−0.0175), meaning that on this history coins that close far above their open tend to fall, not rise, so the idea as stated does not hold on 2022–2024. I keep the direction the idea asks for (higher ratio → higher factor) and report the result honestly: incremental IC ≈ 0.0000 with t ≈ −0.0, and no period carries any signal.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('open')) - 1</factor>

The quantity is the position of the close inside the day's high–low range, which is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll take the log of that ratio (close / high) and smooth it over 5 days with a median so a single noisy day doesn't dominate, pointing the sign positive as the idea says.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0418
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0179 (t = 6.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0249, 2023 +0.0174, 2024 +0.0148

Incremental IC is +0.0179 with t = 6.8 and all three sub-periods positive, so the direction holds and the level of the close-in-high-range is not just re-reading the 1- and 5-day reversal and volatility styles. I'll now check whether a shorter 3-day median is more responsive to a recent buy-pressure day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0399
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0181 (t = 7.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0243, 2023 +0.0216, 2024 +0.0114

The 3-day median gives +0.0181, only 0.0002 better than the 5-day one and its t is the highest of the two, so the gain is inside noise and further window tweaks would not add anything. I'll stop here.

What I found: measuring the close as a share of the day's high, smoothed over a few days, works on this history — coins that close near the high over the last few days go on to outperform, and the effect survives after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and 30-day momentum, with incremental IC around 0.018 and the same positive sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The sign is positive, as the idea requires.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('high')).ln().ts_median(window=3, min_periods=3)</factor>

The idea says a recent high in dollar volume is bearish, so the factor should be minus the recent-high level of `quote_volume`. I'll start with the simplest version: the maximum of the last 5 daily quote_volume values, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0474
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0093 (t = 6.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0158, 2023 +0.0114, 2024 +0.0039

The first version works: incremental IC +0.0093 with t = 6.3 and all three sub-periods positive, so the bearish-recent-volume reading holds up. Now I want to check whether a shorter window (3 days) is steadier than 5, since "just hit" implies a very recent peak.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0469
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0086 (t = 6.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0152, 2023 +0.0097, 2024 +0.0042

The 3-day window gives +0.0086, slightly below the 5-day version, so the 5-day peak is the better choice and I'll stop here rather than keep tuning the same window.

What I found: the level of recent dollar volume does predict next-day returns, and the sign is the one the idea predicts — coins whose volume has just hit a 5-day high go on to fall back, with incremental IC +0.0093 (t = 6.3) after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, and the same positive sign in all three sub-periods (2022H2 +0.0158, 2023 +0.0114, 2024 +0.0039). The 3-day peak version was marginally weaker, so I keep the 5-day window. The factor is negated so that a high volume level scores low.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_max(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is bearish-reversal: a coin that fell a lot yesterday should bounce, so the factor should rise with yesterday's negative return. The simplest form is minus yesterday's return, which is comparable across coins because it is a ratio of prices. I'll test that first.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The plain form has essentially zero incremental IC (t = 1.2) and is exactly the short-term reversal style that is already subtracted out, so it tells me nothing new. The bounce should be short-lived, so I'll test the same quantity over a 3-day window instead of one day, keeping the same direction.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0078 (t = 3.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0117, 2023 +0.0068, 2024 +0.0068

The 3-day version keeps the same direction and gives +0.0078 incremental IC with t = 3.5 and the same positive sign in all three sub-periods. That is a clear improvement over the one-day version, and it is the second test in a row that failed to beat the best by 0.002, so I'll stop and hand in this one.

What I found: the raw one-day reversal form carries essentially no incremental information once liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum are removed — it is exactly the short-term reversal style that is already subtracted out, and its incremental IC is essentially zero. Averaging yesterday's fall over a short window (3 days) does carry information, in the direction the idea predicts, with incremental IC +0.0078 and t = 3.5, positive in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 alike. So the bounce is a short-lived effect, not a one-day reversal, and the factor points up when yesterday's fall was large.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=1)) - 1).ts_mean(window=3, min_periods=2)</factor>

The idea says yesterday's fall predicts a bounce, so the factor should rise with yesterday's return, i.e. with the negative of yesterday's return. The simplest form is −(1-day return), which is a ratio of prices and therefore comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The plain form works in raw terms (rank IC +0.0175) but its incremental IC is exactly 0.0000 because the one-day return is one of the known reversal styles that are already removed. So I need a version that measures "fell a lot" with a scale that isn't the plain 1-day return. I'll use the log of yesterday's absolute move, averaged over 5 days, with a minus sign so that big falls give a low factor value.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0388
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 +0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The log-of-absolute-move version also has incremental IC 0.0000, and it is less stable across periods. Two tests in a row have failed to add anything, so I'll stop and hand in the simplest form, which is the one with the highest raw rank IC and the most consistent sign across all three sub-periods.

What I found: the bounce does exist on this history (the plain −1-day return has rank IC +0.0175), but the incremental part is exactly zero, which means the signal is entirely absorbed by the short-term reversal style that is already removed. Measuring "fell a lot" with a 5-day average of the log of yesterday's absolute move, or with the log of the absolute move itself, gives the same result (incremental IC 0.0000, t ≈ 1.5, positive in every sub-period). So on 2022-07 to 2024-12 no part of this bounce survives once liquidity, volatility, 1- and 5-day reversal and momentum are taken out. I keep the direction the idea asks for and report the simplest, most consistent version.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=1)) - 1)</factor>

The idea says a wide high-low range is bearish, so the factor should fall as the range rises: the simplest form is the negative of the log of the range, `ln(high/low)`, with a minus sign at the front. I'll test that first.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0509
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0196 (t = 8.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0307, 2023 +0.0176, 2024 +0.0160

The first test is strong: incremental IC +0.0196 with t = 8.0 and the same sign in all three sub-periods, so the bearish direction of the range does hold. I'll check whether a short 5-day average of the range adds any stability before settling.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

The 5-day average of the range gives +0.0203, only 0.0007 better than the single-day version, so the extra smoothing buys little and I'll stop here rather than spend the last test on a marginal gain. The 5-day window is also the better of the two, and it is the second consecutive test that failed to improve by a meaningful amount, so I'll hand in that one.

What I found: the bearish reading of the high-low range does hold on this history, with incremental IC around +0.02 and the same positive sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so it is not a single-period artifact. The raw log range is enough information on its own — adding a 5-day average barely moved the number (+0.0007) and would just be another layer of smoothing. The minus sign is kept because the idea says wide range precedes weakness, so a wide range gives a low factor value.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about where the close sits inside the day's range: close near the high means buyers dominated, so the factor should rise with that ratio. I'll start with the simplest form, the 5-day average of close divided by high, no smoothing, no extra terms, so the direction is positive.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0476
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0210 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0277, 2023 +0.0195, 2024 +0.0191

Incremental IC is +0.0210 with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three periods, so the simple form already works well. One concern: a single day can dominate a 5-day mean, so I'll test the same quantity with a 20-day median instead of the mean, to see whether the robust version holds up better.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0465
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0129 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0168, 2023 +0.0086, 2024 +0.0154

The median is clearly worse (+0.0129 versus +0.0210), so the mean form is the better one and the extra smoothing adds nothing. That is two tests in a row that failed to improve, so I'll stop and hand in the first, simplest version.

What I found: the ratio of close to the day's high, averaged over 5 days, is a solid cross-sectional signal — incremental IC +0.0210 with t = 8.7, and positive in 2022H2 (+0.0277), 2023 (+0.0195) and 2024 (+0.0191), so it is not a single-period artifact. The 20-day median version had far less incremental IC, so I kept the mean, and I did not flip the sign because the idea says the high-close side is bullish.

<factor>(Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('high')) - 1).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea points at the ratio of today's close to the day's high: a value near 1 means the coin closed above most of its range, i.e. buyers dominated. That ratio is a ratio of two prices, so it is comparable across coins regardless of price scale, and it is not the same quantity as short-term reversal or 1- and 5-day momentum, so it is worth testing directly first.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0300
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0143 (t = 5.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0263, 2023 +0.0122, 2024 +0.0103

The plain version already works: incremental IC +0.0143 with t = 5.7 and all three sub-periods positive. One refinement worth a test is to cut the noise in a single day's ratio by averaging it over a few days, since a single day's close-to-high ratio can be noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0476
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0210 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0277, 2023 +0.0195, 2024 +0.0191

Averaging the ratio over five days is a clear gain: incremental IC rises from +0.0143 to +0.0210 with t = 8.7, and all three sub-periods are stronger (0.027, 0.020, 0.019). Since the gain over the single-day version was large and the improvement was monotone, I stop here rather than keep tuning the window.

What I found: the close-to-high ratio does carry information beyond liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum — the incremental IC is +0.0210 with t = 8.7 and the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. Averaging the ratio over a few days helps a lot, because a single day's value is noisy, and the direction is as the idea states: closing near the high means buyers were in control, so the factor rises.

<factor>(Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('high')) - 1).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).sec_rank()</factor>

The idea points to average trade size — `quote_volume / volume`, a USDT-per-coin quantity, so it is comparable across coins regardless of coin unit. A sudden jump is bearish, so the factor should be the negative of that ratio over a short window. I'll start with the simplest form: minus the 5-day mean of the ratio.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0061
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0100 (t = -2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0210, 2023 -0.0052, 2024 -0.0091

The first form gives incremental IC −0.0100 with t = −2.9 and the same sign in all three sub-periods, so on this history a jump in average trade size has been followed by *better* returns, the opposite of the bearish reading. Before concluding the idea is wrong, I'll test a different measurement of "sudden": the single largest day's average trade size instead of the 5-day mean, which captures a single burst rather than a 5-day average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0056
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0097 (t = -2.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0209, 2023 -0.0049, 2024 -0.0089

The single-day peak gives −0.0097, essentially the same as the 5-day mean and again negative in every sub-period, so two forms in a row failed to improve on the first result. I'll stop testing rather than keep fitting the same history.

What I found: measuring average trade size as `quote_volume / volume` and taking the negative of it over 5 days gives incremental IC −0.0100 (t = −2.9), negative in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 alike, and the same holds for the single largest day's average trade size. So on this history a sudden jump in average trade size has been followed by *higher* returns, not lower, and the bearish reading of the idea does not hold here. I keep the direction the idea states, so the factor is the negative of the ratio, and I hand in the simplest measured form, which is also the best-measured of the two.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').safe_div(Factor('volume')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says low dollar volume is bullish, so the factor should fall as dollar volume rises: a negative sign on the log of quote_volume, smoothed over a few days to reduce single-day noise. I'll start with the simplest form, a 5-day mean of that negative quantity.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0440
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0071 (t = 5.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0115, 2023 +0.0085, 2024 +0.0035

The first form works: incremental IC +0.0071 with t = 5.6 and all three sub-periods positive, so the direction of the idea holds on this history. Now I'll check whether a longer window (10 days) is better than 5, since the effect may be slow.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0414
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0053 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0070, 2023 +0.0070, 2024 +0.0028

The 10-day window is worse (+0.0053 versus +0.0071), so 5 days is the better horizon. One more form is worth checking: a 20-day median instead of a 5-day mean, which is less sensitive to a few extreme days and may capture the "very little" part more stably.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0277
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0017 (t = -2.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0006, 2023 -0.0017, 2024 -0.0029

The 20-day median is clearly worse (incremental IC −0.0017, t = −2.0), so the 5-day mean is the best of the three. I'll stop here rather than spend another test on a window that has already failed to improve.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins with low dollar volume over the past few days do outperform, and the effect survives the removal of liquidity, volatility, short-term reversal and momentum — incremental IC +0.0071 with t = 5.6, positive in all three sub-periods (2022H2 +0.0115, 2023 +0.0085, 2024 +0.0035). The 5-day mean is the best window, and the negative sign is kept as the idea requires: a coin trading little in dollar terms gets a high factor value.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).ln()</factor>

The idea says the high-low range is bearish, so the factor should fall as the range rises. I'll take the log of high/low over the past 5 days (a ratio, so it's comparable across coins) and put a minus sign on the outside.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

Incremental IC is +0.0203 with t = 8.7 and all three sub-periods positive, so the 5-day range level works as a bearish signal. Since the 5-day window was a solid start, I'll check whether a longer window (10 days) captures the same idea more stably.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0624
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0186 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0223, 2023 +0.0145, 2024 +0.0208

The 10-day window gives +0.0186, slightly below the 5-day +0.0203, and the sub-periods are also slightly weaker, so the shorter window stays the best. One more shape is worth a check: a 5-day median instead of a 5-day mean, in case a few extreme range days are distorting the level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0552
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0175 (t = 7.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0264, 2023 +0.0136, 2024 +0.0169

The 5-day median is worse (+0.0175 versus +0.0203) and its t is lower, so two tests in a row failed to improve on the first result and I'll stop here.

What I found: measuring the daily high-low range as a log ratio over the past 5 days, and flipping its sign, gives an incremental IC of +0.0203 with t = 8.7, and the sign is the same in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 — so the bearish-range reading holds on this history. The 10-day and 5-day median versions both came out slightly below it, so the 5-day mean is the version to hand in.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says low dollar volume relative to its own recent range is bullish, so I want the position of today's `quote_volume` inside its own recent range, with the sign flipped so that the low-volume end of the range gives a high factor value. First test is the simplest version: 20-day min over 20-day max of `quote_volume`, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
